title: Emergent classicality and wavefunction branching in an isolated quantum many-body system
authors: Saúl Pilatowsky-Cameo, Jordan Cotler, Daniel Ranard, C. Jess Riedel
abstract: Decoherence in quantum systems is conventionally modeled as the effect of interactions with an external environment. However, such a prescription excludes isolated many-body systems, which are also expected to display classical behavior at macroscopic scales. In isolated systems, decoherence must emerge internally from microscopic degrees of freedom that are invisible to the macroscopic description. Here we explicitly show that classicality can emerge in such a fashion. We consider a weakly disordered, $3$-local chaotic kicked top of $N$ qubits, where the collective spin sector serves as the macroscopic description, while the microscopic permutation sector acts as an internal bath, decohering the collective spin sector. Starting from closed unitary dynamics, we derive and numerically confirm an effective Lindblad equation for the collective spin variables. In the thermodynamic limit these reduced dynamics converge to a classical chaotic Fokker--Planck equation with vanishingly small diffusion on the spherical phase space, producing a quantum-classical correspondence beyond the Ehrenfest time. The chaotic dynamics evolve the pure many-body wavefunction into continuously branching components associated with distinct classical trajectories. These branches acquire nearly orthogonal microscopic records in the permutation sector, preventing quantum interferences and ensuring the corresponding histories remain consistent.
summary: This work demonstrates that classical behavior can emerge in isolated quantum systems by treating internal microscopic degrees of freedom as an effective bath. Using a kicked top model, the authors derive an effective Lindblad equation whose classical limit is a chaotic Fokker-Planck equation. This shows that quantum evolution naturally branches into distinct classical histories without external environmental coupling.
main_problem: To explain how classical behavior emerges in isolated quantum many-body systems without relying on coupling to an external environment.
main_result: Classicality emerges internally from microscopic degrees of freedom, leading to reduced dynamics that converge to a classical chaotic Fokker-Planck equation beyond the Ehrenfest time.
method: The authors derive an effective Lindblad equation for the macroscopic spin sector by tracing out the microscopic permutation sector, and analyze the resulting quantum-classical correspondence.
model_or_system: The model is a weakly disordered, 3-local chaotic kicked top of N qubits, decomposed into a macroscopic collective spin sector (S) and a microscopic permutation sector (P) acting as an internal bath.
key_observables: Classicality, quantum-classical correspondence, wavefunction branching, and the fidelity of microscopic records.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($\varepsilon$), system size ($N$), and the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The standard decoherence theory assumption of coupling to an external environment is bypassed; the system-bath decomposition is emergent.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates decoherence and classicality in the spin sector; Figure 2 shows the effective Lindblad dynamics and rate convergence.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the internal mechanism for decoherence in isolated systems, derives the effective dynamics via a Lindblad equation, confirms the convergence to a classical Fokker-Planck equation, and analyzes wavefunction branching using consistent histories.
why_interesting: It provides a mechanism for quantum-to-classical transition entirely within the system's Hamiltonian structure, which is highly relevant for understanding complex quantum dynamics in isolated materials.

The disorder in the Hamiltonian scrambles the singlets throughout, leading to microscopically distinct branches that cannot interfere in collective observables, so their superposition is indistinguishable from a classical mixture.
